category.label: Fish Oil
category.comparisonNote: EPA+DHA and total fish-oil mass are recorded separately. Compare the chemical form and actual label serving alongside cost.

guide.title: Fish oil: EPA+DHA, outcomes and the prescription distinction
guide.summary: Total fish-oil mass is not the same as the amount of EPA and DHA. More oil does not by itself establish greater benefit.
guide.evidence: Omega-3 research differs by population and preparation. VITAL did not show a significant reduction in its primary cardiovascular or cancer outcomes with the tested marine omega-3 supplement.
guide.limitations: Specific prescription formulations, high-risk patients and treatment of high triglycerides address different questions from routine retail supplementation.
guide.catalogReading: Use verified EPA+DHA per label serving and cost per common active amount. Keep total oil, chemical form, serving count and stock status visible.
guide.safety: Discuss use with a clinician when taking anticoagulants or considering high doses. High-dose trials have raised atrial-fibrillation concerns in some settings.
guide.author: Supplement Research editorial synthesis
bodySteps: Digestion releases fatty acids from dietary oils.
Intestinal cells package absorbed fats into transport particles that reach the circulation through lymph.
EPA and DHA enter tissue lipids and cell membranes and contribute to signalling pathways.
guide.treatment: Prescription omega-3 medicines can treat high triglycerides under medical care. Retail fish oil is not an interchangeable prescription or a cure for heart disease.
guide.whoMayBenefit: People with a clinician-established indication; those with low fish intake can first review food and suitable alternative omega-3 sources.
guide.routineUse: No blanket recommendation that every healthy adult needs fish-oil capsules. Dietary context and the clinical goal matter.

whoCanConsider: Adults with persistently low oily-fish intake who are reviewing options for dietary EPA and DHA.
People for whom food changes are impractical and a suitable clearly labelled product meets an assessed nutritional preference.
whoShouldReview: Fish allergy requires product-specific suitability review.
Anticoagulant use or a history of atrial fibrillation warrants discussion before supplementation, particularly stronger products.
High triglycerides or cardiovascular disease needs medical assessment; ordinary retail fish oil does not substitute for prescription treatment.

dos.title: Find EPA and DHA
dos.detail: Use verified EPA+DHA per label serving and units per serving to compare meaningful active-content costs.

dos.title: Check diet and overlap
dos.detail: Review fish intake, other omega-3 products and relevant medicines before adding another product.

donts.title: Don't compare total oil alone
donts.detail: A large fish-oil headline does not establish the EPA+DHA amount delivered by a serving.

donts.title: Don't substitute for a prescription
donts.detail: Retail fish oil is not interchangeable with a condition-specific prescription omega-3 medicine.

intakeGuide.summary: There is no established US adult RDA for EPA+DHA. The ALA reference is a different omega-3 and must not become a fish-oil target.
notes: No automatic dose increase is assigned for training frequency or experience.

medicalGuide.summary: Condition-specific evidence, separate from sports benefits and purchase priority.

conditions.findings: Prescription omega-3 medicines have a clinical role. Retail fish oil is not interchangeable; the exact prescription formulation and indication matter.
conditions.limits: Prescription omega-3 medicines can treat high triglycerides under medical care. Retail fish oil is not an interchangeable prescription or a cure for heart disease.

conditions.findings: Benefits vary by population and formulation; results from a specific prescription cannot be transferred to every fish-oil capsule.

pathway.title: From oil digestion to EPA and DHA in tissues
pathway.summary: EPA and DHA travel through normal fat digestion and lipoprotein transport before contributing to tissue lipids and signalling pathways.

steps.label: Digestion releases oil breakdown products
steps.detail: Intestinal digestion hydrolyses dietary oils into fatty acids and other absorbable lipid products.

steps.label: Micelles deliver fats for absorption
steps.detail: Bile-containing micelles help lipid digestion products reach and enter intestinal cells.

steps.label: Chylomicrons enter lymph then blood
steps.detail: Intestinal cells package absorbed fats into chylomicrons, which reach the circulation through lymph.

steps.label: Tissues incorporate EPA and DHA
steps.detail: EPA and DHA enter tissue lipids; omega-3s contribute to membranes and the production of signalling molecules.

pathway.caveat: A membrane or signalling role does not prove that every fish-oil product prevents disease. EPA and DHA content matters more than total oil mass.
